chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Husayn ibn Umar ibn Yazeed, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When the two merchants are truthful, blessings are bestowed upon them. And when they lie and betray, no blessings are bestowed upon them. And they both have the option (to cancel the deal) as long as they have not separated. So if they differ, the word is the word of the owner of the goods, or they both leave it.'

key_terms.الْخِيَار: the option / right to choose (to accept or cancel)
key_terms.يَتَتَارَكَا: they both leave / cancel the deal

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on truthfulness in trade and the right to cancel a deal before separation?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the spiritual dimension of commerce, linking material transaction integrity to divine barakah, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence on market ethics. It codifies the 'Option of the Session' (Khiyar al-Majlis), granting parties the right to rescind the deal before physical separation, thereby preventing disputes arising from post-sale regret or hidden defects. The ruling that the seller's word prevails in case of disagreement reflects the practical legal presumption of ownership and knowledge held by the vendor.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Al Husayn Bin Umar Bin Yazeed, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When the two merchants (buyer and seller) are both truthful, there would be Blessings for both of them. So when they are both liars, and betrayers, there would be no Blessings for both of them, and they are both with the choice (not to transact) for as long as they do not separate (from each other). So if they differ, so the (final) word is the word of the owner of the item, or they both leave it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Al-Husayn ‘Umar ibn Yazid from his father, who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If the two business people speak the truth the transaction is a blessing for them; but if they speak lies and cheat, it does not become a blessing for them. They have the choice to keep or dismiss the transaction as long as they you must not depart each other. After they depart the words of the owner of merchandise are accepted or they can mutually agree to dismiss the transaction.’”
